questions.question: The catalogue joins the ground, so every /observe session reads it. The planned '0.33 counterpart' column would put 0.33 method names (read_bytes, write_atomic, get_file_info, head, ...) in front of each session, the exact priming the first /observe run traced to a register row (BK-485 dossier). Where does the omission check live?

options.label: Out of the ground (Recommended)
options.description: catalogue.md has no 0.33 column. The entry-to-0.33 mapping stays in BK-493's dossier (already there) and RFC-0026 records that the check was run. Sessions see intents only; D8's comparison pass still has the mapping.

options.label: Keep it in the catalogue
options.description: As planned in the dossier's Status step 3. One table holds everything, but every session reads 0.33's method names, against S1 and the lesson from the exists run.

options.label: Separate non-ground file
options.description: A sibling file, e.g. sdd/observe/catalogue-033.md, not on the register. Keeps the mapping next to the catalogue for the D8 pass, at the cost of a second table to keep in step.

questions.question: Spec 053 states v1's public operations as exactly the catalogue's entries. STORE-008 (spec 001) and ASYNC-046 (spec 029) list 0.33's full surface. Does spec 053 supersede them under RFC-0024 D7?

options.label: Supersede both (Recommended)
options.description: Spec 053 names STORE-008 and ASYNC-046 as superseded; specs 001 and 029 get the one-line D7 header, as spec 004 did for 052. No 0.33 clause text changes.

options.label: Supersede nothing
options.description: The surface lists stay live until each operation's flow supersedes its method sections. Spec 001/029 untouched, but two live clauses then contradict spec 053 on what the surface is.

questions.question: Spec 053's clauses (exact surface, async twin, optional entries gated) can only fail against a v1 Store, which does not exist. What goes under 'Tested against' for the draft?

options.label: None, reason in Notes (Recommended)
options.description: 'None.' with a Note that each clause's witness is a public surface of the v1 API, checked once the API flow builds one (R4: binds code only from then). Honest; reviewers will flag SPEC-DESIGN's Ready item 2, which I answer with R4.

options.label: Add a catalogue table check
options.description: A small test parsing catalogue.md (unique contiguous IDs, allowed column values, every use case served by an entry). It checks the table, not spec 053's clauses, so it adds a guard but no clause coverage.

OP-05's scope (research Q2): the vendor stores and OpenDAL attach the same conditions (if-match, if-absent, version) to read, delete, copy and rename as well as write, and OpenDAL's conditional-operations spec defines them once for all. How should the catalogue treat conditions?

options.label: Write-only, rest excluded (Recommended)
options.description: OP-05 stays 'write only if absent or unchanged' (N-17). Conditional read, delete, copy and move are listed as not in v1. OP-05's session gets OpenDAL's spec as prior art (no silent drop, atomic with commit). A later need reopens the catalogue.

options.label: One condition entry
options.description: OP-05 becomes 'condition an operation': its session designs the condition model once and decides which entries accept it. Matches OpenDAL, but it is a modifier, not an intent, so it bends one-entry-per-intent and couples OP-05 to five other sessions.

options.label: Write-only + conditional read
options.description: OP-05 stays write-only and a new v1 entry covers a read that is skipped or pinned unless unchanged (5/10 offer it). Delete, copy and move conditions excluded.

questions.question: Listing (research Q2): the least agreed cut. gocloud, object_store and pyarrow use one listing call with options; fsspec and cloudpathlib split list, walk and glob. Only fsspec has a depth limit, and on object stores depth costs a full subtree listing. What happens to OP-06/07/08?

options.label: Keep three, keep depth (Recommended)
options.description: As drafted, and as you chose ('possibly limited by depth'). The cost note goes to OP-07's session. Matches fsspec and cloudpathlib; each session designs one shape.

options.label: Keep three, drop depth
options.description: OP-07 becomes 'walk a subtree' with no depth limit, which only fsspec offers. N-06 loses 'or up to a depth'.

options.label: Merge into one listing
options.description: One entry 'list keys under a folder' with depth and pattern as options (gocloud, object_store, pyarrow style). Fewer sessions; one session carries three questions.

questions.question: Operations the comparables offer that no entry covers (research Q1). Which become catalogue entries? Unless you say otherwise, the ones you leave unticked are recorded as not in v1. Separately: batch delete, abort of a streamed write, multi-range read and delete guardrails go in as forms of OP-10, OP-03, OP-02 and OP-11, and versioned access is recorded as not in v1.

options.label: Presigned URL, optional
options.description: 8/10 offer it. Time-limited access without credentials. Local, SFTP and Memory cannot, so it would be a third optional entry, gated like OP-19 and OP-20.

options.label: System properties in OP-20
options.description: 7/10 offer them. Content type, cache control and encoding next to user metadata. OP-20 widens to 'item metadata: user and system properties', still optional.

options.label: Identity token in OP-09
options.description: 6/10 offer one. Inspect's info includes an opaque token (ETag or version, never a content hash), which OP-05's 'if unchanged' needs anyway. No new entry; N-08 widens.

options.label: Append, optional
options.description: 6/10 offer it, always gated and sometimes emulated (s3fs re-uploads). For logs and row appends. It would be a fourth optional entry.

questions.question: RFC-0026 Open Question 2: the research lists the shared decisions comparables most often had to retrofit: `..` containment (spec 052 already decides it), missing-key delete, no silent ignore of an unsupported option, exception typing, sync/async parity, retry tied to idempotency, behaviour on exception mid-write. Does spec 053 take any now?

options.label: Surface only, list as inputs (Recommended)
options.description: Spec 053 keeps its four surface clauses (D5: the rest grows from read()). The list goes into the research doc's filing note and RFC-0026 OQ2 as input for read()'s session and each later one.

options.label: Add 'no silent no-op'
options.description: Spec 053 also says that an operation a store cannot carry out is never reported as done (the pyarrow/cloudpathlib/fsspec pitfall). That is a single-call claim, so spec 053 would hold two kinds of truth, against SPEC-DESIGN Rule 2.

options.label: Open a shared-decisions item
options.description: A new backlog item for a cross-operation layer (errors, retries, closing, conditions), designed before or alongside read(). That would change D5, so it needs its own RFC.

questions.question: OPS-003/004 define 'offers' as operations carrying out an entry's intent on a store. A witness needs a call, so these are single-call clauses inside a structure spec (SPEC-DESIGN Rule 2). How should this be fixed?

options.label: Offer = declared set (Recommended)
options.description: Redefine 'offers' as the entries a store's OP-18 answer names. OPS-003/004 then constrain that declared set, so a witness is one store's state and the spec stays structure. That an offered entry actually works goes to the entry's own spec. Keeps the decision recorded in the logs that 053 holds the v1/optional gate.

options.label: Move to OP-18's spec
options.description: Drop OPS-003/004 from 053, which keeps only OPS-001/002 (pure surface). The gate then lives only in the catalogue's Offer column until OP-18's session specifies it. This reverses the decision that 053 holds the gate.

options.label: Keep, classify as mixed
options.description: Leave the clauses as they are and note the two kinds in the RFC. This openly breaks Rule 2 ('one kind per spec').

questions.question: Research § 3 and the register header admit a flow's output only 'once its spec and formal model are accepted'. Spec 053 and the catalogue join with no formal model, and RFC-0026 does not address this. How should this be fixed?

options.label: State the exception (Recommended)
options.description: RFC-0026 C4 says step 4b's output joins without a formal model: its clauses quantify over a finite table and a surface no model can bridge to until v1 exists, so a model would only restate the table. The register header gets a pointer to C4.

options.label: Write an Alloy model
options.description: Add a small Alloy model of OPS-001 to OPS-004 (operations, entries, forms, stores) and register it as ground. It stays unbridged until a v1 surface exists, so it informs review but governs nothing. Adds a file and its CI check to this PR.

questions.question: The catalogue's Session column holds per-entry project status in a ground file, so every entry's flow would have to edit ground outside the catalogue's own flow (research § 3: 'never changes ground on the side'). How should this be fixed?

options.label: Drop the column (Recommended)
options.description: Remove Session. An entry's status then comes from its backlog item and the ground register row its spec gets when admitted. Spec 053's Notes bullet that justifies the table by 'status changes' is rewritten.

options.label: Keep it, sanction the edit
options.description: Keep the column, and have RFC-0026 C2 state that each entry's flow sets its own Session cell as part of admission, the same way it adds its register row. The status stays in the ground file every session reads.

ChatGPT F-02: OP-05 'write if absent or if unchanged' is `v1` (every store), but 'unchanged' needs a change token that N-08 says only some backends offer. How should OP-05 handle this?

options.label: Keep v1, profile (Recommended)
options.description: OP-05 stays `v1`. Its own design session declares a profile: where a backend has no token, 'if unchanged' refuses with a typed error and never quietly does a non-atomic check. The catalogue gets one sentence linking OP-05 to OP-09's token. This fits spec 053's Notes on variation inside an entry.

options.label: Split OP-05
options.description: 'If absent' stays `v1` as OP-05, and 'if unchanged' becomes a new optional entry, OP-25, available only where the backend declares a token. This makes the gate visible in the catalogue, but it reverses 'one entry per intent' for conditional writes.

options.label: Token becomes v1
options.description: Every backend must provide a change token, so OP-05 works in full everywhere. Local and SFTP have no reliable native token, so this commits their drivers to building one.

questions.question: ChatGPT F-01/F-07: OP-22 (native address) and OP-23 (native client) are `v1`, yet a backend like Memory may have neither a native client nor a meaningful native address. Should they stay `v1`?

options.label: Make both optional (Recommended)
options.description: OP-22 and OP-23 become optional: only a store whose backend declares them offers them. They are escape hatches outside the library's guarantees, so gating them is honest. OP-24 (health) stays `v1`; what a health check promises is its own session's decision.

options.label: Keep v1, profile
options.description: Both stay `v1`, and each session declares what a backend without a client or address answers (for example, a typed 'not available'). The catalogue doesn't change.

options.label: OP-23 optional only
options.description: Only OP-23 (native client) becomes optional. OP-22 stays `v1`, because every backend can map a key to some native form, even if only a string.
